definitions.package_identity: The exact npm package (name + version in package.json) that carries the console. The console ships as part of the CURRENT single Next.js package — no new component, no new topology, no separate console package (design §15). The harness compares package.json on disk against this registry and fails closed on any drift.
definitions.ships_within: The deployment component whose route surface and runtime package carry the console routes. PC-006 adds no component: the console routes extend web-api-boundary's route_surface (the D-1 governed-change precedent — a route_surface extension recorded in deploy/contracts/components.json together with the topology.md contract-evolution entry).
definitions.console_route_surface: The complete inventory of console routes: the 26 console pages under src/app/console/**/page.tsx plus the 10 console API boundary routes under src/app/api/console/**/route.ts. STATIC routes are mirrored into deploy/contracts/components.json web-api-boundary route_surface (its flat-route convention cannot express dynamic path segments); DYNAMIC routes (the three [param] routes) are recorded ONLY here, where the harness validates them against the filesystem, the CONSOLE_REGISTRY source hrefs and — when a build output is present — the build's app-path-routes manifest.
definitions.provider_bindings: The provider-binding truth for the console deployment contract (design §15): each provider of the closed six-provider set records either CONNECTED (with a repository evidence reference, a verification timestamp and a provenance statement) or UNBOUND (explicit, with null evidence fields and the requirement that live provider evidence must precede any production claim). No other status value exists.
definitions.invariants: The honesty rules the verification harness enforces mechanically over this registry. They are the machine contract for the two-gate separation (design §15): repository verification is never deployment verification.

console_route_surface.dynamic_route_representation: Dynamic path segments ([paymentId], [checkoutId]) are recorded in this registry only. deploy/contracts/components.json route_surface uses the validator's flat static-route convention (entries match the route regex of scripts/validate_deployment.py, which cannot express brackets); the static console routes are mirrored there and the dynamic routes are proven here, against the same filesystem and registry sources.
console_route_surface.route_availability_note: Route availability at PC-006 is REPOSITORY availability: every route maps to an existing page/route source file, equals the frozen CONSOLE_REGISTRY hrefs (src/lib/console/registry.ts), and — when a build output is present — appears in the build's app-path-routes manifest. This is not a claim that any route is deployed or serving traffic anywhere.

environment_requirements.environment_chain: PAYSWAP_ENV (server process environment only; exact allowlist sandbox | production; unset/empty/invalid fail-safes to sandbox — never to production) resolved through the frozen src/lib/environment.ts
environment_requirements.startup_validation: src/lib/startup-config.ts validateStartupConfig() — sandbox requires nothing beyond the environment itself; production requires the four named configuration names (PAYSWAP_DATABASE_URL, PAYSWAP_QUEUE_URL, PAYSWAP_EVIDENCE_STORE_URL, PAYSWAP_RAIL_ADAPTERS_URL) and fails closed (ids only, never values)
environment_requirements.console_adds_no_configuration: The console program added NO externally configurable value (spec/deployment/configuration.md unchanged by PC-001..PC-006). The console's environment scope is server-derived only (the PC-001 no-input authority chain); there is no client-side environment switching anywhere in the console.
environment_requirements.fail_safe_sandbox: The console can therefore only ever render in sandbox semantics unless a deployment injects the production configuration through the documented chain — the same F1-F8 rules that govern the whole package.

invariants.closed_provider_set: The provider set is exactly the design §15 set — vercel (runtime host), database, queue, cloudflare, observability, github — each present exactly once. Extending the set is a governed change to this registry together with spec/deployment/console-deployment.md and the design baseline.
invariants.connected_requires_full_evidence: binding_status CONNECTED requires a non-null evidence_reference that resolves to an EXISTING repository file, a non-empty verification_timestamp, and a non-empty provenance statement. A CONNECTED entry without all three fails closed in the harness.
invariants.unbound_is_explicit: binding_status UNBOUND requires null evidence_reference, null verification_timestamp, null provenance, and a non-empty requirement statement recording that live provider evidence must precede any production claim.
invariants.closed_status_vocabulary: binding_status is exactly one of CONNECTED | UNBOUND. No other value (no 'assumed', no 'partial', no 'probably') may appear.
invariants.no_fake_bindings: No provider may be marked CONNECTED without a repository evidence reference that records the connection. The harness never verifies liveness of any provider — it verifies the HONESTY of the recorded state. Flipping an UNBOUND provider to CONNECTED is a governed change that attaches live provider evidence from the operator (evidence reference + timestamp + provenance), updates this registry, spec/deployment/console-deployment.md and the evidence document, and re-runs scripts/test_console_deployment.mjs.
invariants.repository_verification_is_not_deploymen: A passing verification harness proves REPOSITORY facts only — package identity, contract agreement, route availability in source and build output, and the honesty of the recorded binding state. It is NOT production proof: no route is claimed deployed, no provider is claimed serving, and no production readiness is inferred (environments.md F8; production-readiness.md §1 hard boundary; design §15 two-gate separation). This registry and its harness sit BELOW the provider-binding gate in the design §15 chain — they can never substitute for it.
